chunks: And by this chain of narrators, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynahh and Hariz, from Zurarah, from one of them both (peace be upon them both), who said:
'Nothing invalidates the wudu except what exits from your two ends, or sleep.'

key_terms.النَّوْمُ: sleep — cited alongside emissions as one of only two causes of wudu-nullification in Shia fiqh
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu — ritual ablution required before salat and other acts of worship
key_terms.طَرَفَيْكَ: your two ends — the two lower orifices (front and back private parts); the dual grammatical form specifies both exits precisely
key_terms.يَنْقُضُ: to break/invalidate — the technical fiqh term for nullifying a state of ritual purity (taharah)

ai.seo_question: What nullifies wudu (ritual ablution) according to Shia hadith from the Imams (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Zurarah from Imam al-Baqir or al-Sadiq (AS), establishes the foundational Shia jurisprudential ruling that only two categories of events nullify wudu: emissions from the two lower orifices (front and back private parts), and sleep. This is among the most frequently cited narrations in Shia fiqh on the law of ritual purity (taharah), and its restrictive enumeration distinguishes the Shia position from some other schools.
